title: Baby Water Play: Splash & Pour
strapline: Splash, dip, pour and squeeze — warm water and a baby discovering they can make it move.
intent: Warm, shallow water gives babies a rich, safe sensory experience of wet, cool, splash and flow to explore with their whole bodies.
Discovering that a slap makes a splash, or a squeezed sponge makes it rain, builds early cause-and-effect and joyful, repeatable control.
Grasping, tipping and squeezing cups, sponges and toys develops hand strength, coordination and grip.
Water play is naturally calming and absorbing, supporting babies to regulate and settle as they explore.
Sharing the splashes and pours with a warm adult turns exploration into connection, delight and early talk.
implementation: Offer a shallow tray or tuff spot of warm water with cups, sponges, funnels and floating toys, always within close reach and supervision.
Follow the baby's lead — let them splash, dip, mouth and pour without hurrying or correcting.
Name the cause and effect gently: 'you splashed — big splash!', 'squeeze the sponge — it's raining!'
Keep it warm, safe and never unattended, and be ready to swap for a calming pace if a baby is unsettled.
Add simple treasures — a floating duck, a jug that trickles, a colander that pours — to invite new discoveries.
Narrate warmly what the baby sees, hears and does, sharing their delight.
key_questions: You splashed — what a big splash!
Squeeze the sponge — look, it's raining!
Where did the water go when you poured it?
Can you catch the little duck?
That felt cool, didn't it — shall we do it again?

impact.text: Babies explore wet, cool, splash and flow with their whole bodies and all their senses.
Babies discover that a slap makes a splash and a squeeze makes it rain — early cause and effect.
Babies grasp, tip and squeeze cups and sponges, building hand strength and grip.
Water play soothes and absorbs, helping babies settle and regulate with a calm adult close by.
Babies share the splashes and pours with a warm adult through gesture, gaze and first sounds.

enhancements: A floating duck, a trickling jug and a colander that pours to invite new discoveries.
Warm coloured water on a tuff spot for a change of sensation.
Sponges, funnels and cups of different sizes for filling and emptying.
A calmer, slower session ready for any baby who needs soothing rather than splashing.
Ice cubes to chase and melt in warm water on a hot day.

playing_exploring: Babies explore the water freely with hands, mouth and whole body, at their own pace.
active_learning: Babies repeat a splash or a squeeze again and again, absorbed in making it happen.
creating_thinking: Babies begin to connect their own action to the splash or trickle it creates, and try it another way.
